content.text:
This confirms: the only substantive changes to `isAtom`/`getArity`/`getArg` across the entire history are cosmetic (renaming, reformatting) until the actual bugfix commit a7f8831 added the missing `Z3_QUANTIFIER_AST` case and the `Preconditions` guards. The buggy `default: return true` fallthrough (which incorrectly treats quantifiers as atoms) existed unchanged since the file's introduction at the root commit `2b20287`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 2b20287b1767d5736128f8ac2749328b2458ef63

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix in a7f8831 modifies `Z3UnsafeFormulaManager.isAtom`, `getArity`, and `getArg`, adding a `case Z3_QUANTIFIER_AST: return false;` branch and `Preconditions.checkArgument(... == Z3_APP_AST)` guards. I traced the full history of `Z3UnsafeFormulaManager.java` with `git log -p --follow`, checking every commit that touched the `isAtom` switch statement (`319e9c3`, `05afb71`, `b0bddeb`). All of these were purely cosmetic (renaming `nonAtomicOpTypes` → `NON_ATOMIC_OP_TYPES`, switching `HashSet`→`ImmutableSet`, reformatting indentation) — none of them changed the actual logic or removed a previously-existing quantifier handling.

**(2) Root cause:** I then checked the file as it was first added, in the repository's root commit `2b20287` ("Big scary changelist for moving the solver-specific files into a separate changelist", Aug 24, 2015). At that point `isAtom` already had the exact same buggy structure: a `switch` on `astKind` with only a `Z3_APP_AST` case and a `default: return true` fallback, and `getArity`/`getArg` unconditionally called `get_app_num_args`/`get_app_arg` without checking the AST kind at all. Since `Z3_QUANTIFIER_AST` falls into `default`, any quantified formula (forall/exists) was incorrectly classified as an atom, and calling `getArity`/`getName` on it would silently call the wrong native API instead of failing.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** `git log --oneline` and `git rev-list --parents 2b20287` show this commit has no parent — it is the root of the repository's tracked history (159 commits total). The bug is orthogonal/unrelated to any later change; other parts of the code (`Z3QuantifiedFormulaManager.isQuantifier`, `Z3UnsafeFormulaManager.isQuantification`) *did* correctly check for `Z3_QUANTIFIER_AST` from the same root commit onward, showing the developers knew quantifiers had a distinct AST kind — they simply forgot to add that check in `isAtom`/`getArity`/`getArg`. The bug remained latent until commit `3661e14` added the `testIntrospectionForall`/`testIntrospectionExists` tests (with a Z3-skip workaround for the known failure), and was finally fixed in `a7f8831`.

**Uncertainty:** Since `2b20287` is the earliest commit in this repository's history (an import from a larger CPAchecker SVN repo), I cannot verify whether the bug originated even earlier in the pre-import history that isn't available here. Within the scope of this repository, however, the omission is present from the very first commit and was never altered until the fix — so no intermediate commit "introduced" a regression; the code was wrong from the start.
